---
title: "Academic Reporting"
format: html
---

## Citation

Pessina ALR, Garcia-Neto M (2026). PGM: Practical Growth Modeling for jamovi \[Version x.x.x\]. doi: [10.5281/zenodo.15764773](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15764773)

***The jamovi project [@jamovi]*** **and *The R project*[@R] should also be cited.** We also encourage authors to cite the packages and references used in the module’s analyses:

- minpack.lm [@nlsLM]
- nlme [@nlme]

## Recommended information

An academic report should identify:

- the PGM version;
- the jamovi version;
- the selected growth equation;
- the equation parametrization;
- the response and time units;
- the number of observations;
- the number of subjects, when longitudinal;
- the estimation framework;
- the random-effects structure;
- the residual variance structure;
- the residual correlation structure;
- the estimation method;
- the model-comparison criteria;
- the residual diagnostics examined.

## Ordinary nonlinear model

A possible methods statement is:

> Growth trajectories were fitted using the PGM module for jamovi. The \[[Richards\]]{.underline} growth equation was estimated by nonlinear least squares, with initial optimization performed using the Levenberg--Marquardt algorithm. Model adequacy was evaluated using parameter estimates, information criteria, prediction-error measures, and residual diagnostics.

## Generalized nonlinear least squares

When a variance function is included:

> Growth trajectories were fitted using the PGM module for jamovi. The \[[Richards\]]{.underline} growth equation was estimated by nonlinear least squares, with initial optimization performed using the Levenberg--Marquardt algorithm. The resulting estimates were used to initialize a generalized nonlinear least-squares model with a [\[power/exponential/constant-plus-power\]]{.underline} residual variance function based on the fitted response.

## Nonlinear mixed-effects model

For longitudinal data:

> Growth trajectories were fitted using the PGM module for jamovi. Repeated growth measurements were analyzed using a nonlinear mixed-effects model. Population growth parameters were represented by fixed effects, and between-subject variation in the asymptotic parameter was represented by a random effect. Parameters were estimated by maximum likelihood after initialization using a Levenberg--Marquardt nonlinear fit.

### Residual autocorrelation

When applicable:

> Within-subject residual dependence was modeled using a first-order [\[AR(1)/CAR(1)\]]{.underline} correlation structure.

For CAR(1), the report may clarify:

> Correlation was modeled as a function of the actual temporal distance between observations.

### Heteroscedasticity

When applicable:

> Residual variance was modeled as a [\[power/exponential/constant-plus-power\]]{.underline} function of the absolute fitted response.

## Model comparison

A possible statement is:

> Candidate specifications were compared using [\[AIC/AICc\]]{.underline} and BIC, together with residual diagnostics and biological plausibility of the estimated parameters. Information criteria were compared only across models fitted to the same response observations.

## Derived growth descriptors

When reporting derivative-based descriptors:

> Derived growth values and times were calculated from the fitted growth function and its derivatives, presented as point estimates. These quantities were treated as model-based geometric descriptors.

## Tables

### Parameter tables

- estimate;
- standard error;
- confidence interval;
- parameter unit;
- model parametrization.

### Model-comparison tables

- model;
- variance structure;
- correlation structure;
- random-effects structure;
- number of observations;
- information criteria;
- relevant error metrics.

## Figures

### Growth-curve figures

- observed data;
- fitted trajectory;
- response and time units;
- group or subject definition;
- critical-point labels, when used.

### Residual figures

Residual figures should be reported or summarized whenever model assumptions are important to the conclusions.
